text:
maria: Quick cost-vs-quality snapshot for Kairo9b bring-up. Ran short INT4/INT6/FP16 sweep on a GTN product slice. TL;DR: INT4 ~45% token-cost savings, but recall drop on long-form QA (~6-8% absolute). Sharing run notes + recommendations.

maria: Raw numbers (pilot slice, ~1.2k queries, 90th pct length ~720 tokens):
```
mode    | tokens/sec | $/1M tokens (rel) | long-QA recall | latency p95
FP16    | 1.00x      | $1.00             | baseline 0.00%  | 220ms
INT6    | 0.92x      | $0.78             | -1.5%           | 210ms
INT4    | 0.75x      | $0.55             | -6.7%           | 195ms
```

maria: Notes: INT4 throughput drops a bit (kernel efficiency + dequant overhead) so typical latency improved slightly but quality regressed for multi-step retrieval/QA where chain-of-thought matters.

ken: Nice. Where were these runs executed? sample/bench config?

maria: Dedicated infra (4x A100 equiv), batching tuned to ~80ms window, priming preserved. Sample = GTN feedback slice (mix of short chat + long QA weighted to product traffic).

aisha: @maria can you clarify what "recall" means here — are we missing citations or whole answers? user-visible impact?

maria: Good q. Recall = span-level match vs gold in our retrieval-aug QA eval. In practice INT4 tends to truncate or drop footnote/context in 2-3 turn threads => shorter answers and missed citations (higher hallucination risk on edge cases). For discovery/search use-cases visible drop; for short casual chat it's fine.

eval-bot: :warning: regression-detected: long-form-recall decreased 6.7% vs FP16 on slice "gtn-longforms" (p<0.01)

ken: Suggest hybrid routing: default INT4 for <=256 token prompts, INT6 for 256-1024, FP16 fallback for critical queries or on regression signal. Easy to implement with per-route model policy.

maria: Agreed. Proposed rollout config:
```json
{
  "routes": [
    {"max_prompt_len": 256, "model": "kairo9b-int4", "traffic_pct": 60},
    {"min_prompt_len": 257, "max_prompt_len": 1024, "model": "kairo9b-int6", "traffic_pct": 35},
    {"critical": true, "model": "kairo9b-fp16", "traffic_pct": 5}
  ]
}
```

maria: Canary plan: start 5% global, but concentrate that 5% on long-form traffic (where regression most likely). Monitor recall, hallucination rate, and conversational NPS. If recall drop >3% on canary, rollback INT4.

aisha: That seems sensible. What's the ballpark cost impact if we move 50% of short traffic to INT4?

maria: Back-of-envelope: moving 50% short traffic to INT4 => ~18-22% total token-cost reduction across product (shorts are ~40% of tokens). For 1M tokens baseline $1.0 -> new blended ~$0.78. Concrete: ~$220k -> ~$171k per month for current volume (very approximate).

ken: Can we reduce recall hit with light prompt/priming changes? e.g. stronger retrieval context, pointer-based prompts?

maria: Yes — reducing model decoding burden helps. Quick wins: 1) include top-5 retrieved context reliably, 2) explicit instruction to prefer longer answers for evidence, 3) larger retrieval windows for long-form paths. These reduce the INT4 recall gap by ~2-3% in small tests.

aisha: Ok let's capture this as recommended playbook for GTN: 1) Hybrid routing by prompt length, 2) Focused canary on long-form, 3) Prompt/retrieval improvements, 4) Threshold-based rollback (recall drop >3%). I'll loop in growth for observability.

maria: I'll open the canary PR with rollout config + eval hooks and attach the detailed logs.

ken: :thumbsup: thanks.

aisha: Thanks team — useful and pragmatic.
